title: In 2 macaques with V1, V4 and IT arrays and 22,248 THINGS images, IT spectra did not decay faster than V1; V1 decay depended on coverage, and IT gained V4-predicted human-similarity concept variance
abstract: Earlier SCI studies found faster-decaying cross-validated PCA response spectra (larger exponent alpha) in higher mouse visual areas, with the extra variance off the VISp stimulus axes. A parallel study found no such compression in two small macaque data sets. We tested this in the THINGS Ventral-stream Spiking Dataset: multi-unit activity from V1, V4 and IT arrays recorded together in 2 macaques, 22,248 single-presentation images (1,854 concepts x 12 exemplars) and 100 test images x 30 repeats. With 100 reliable channels and noise-corrected spectra, alpha (ranks 2-30) was 1.34, 1.12, 1.20 (monkey N) and 1.24, 1.18, 1.11 (monkey F) for V1, V4, IT; IT minus V1 was -0.14 and -0.12 (concept-bootstrap intervals about +/-0.01). An array-level model gave -0.16 per hierarchy level (-0.31 to -0.02); the mouse effect is about +0.15. However, V1 alpha fell from 1.55 to 1.29 (N) and 1.52 to 1.14 (F) when 28 channels came from 7 arrays instead of 1, while IT did not change; at the widest V1 coverage V1 and IT differed by less than 0.1, so a small compression relative to a fully covered V1 is not excluded. IT variance lay off the V1 image axes (top 10 V1 axes held 21% and 19% of IT signal against 75% and 59% for IT axes). The between-concept share of signal rose from 0.21 to 0.41 (N) and 0.19 to 0.35 (F). A 49-D human similarity embedding explained 41% to 68% (N) and 42% to 52% (F) of between-concept variance from V1 to IT. V4 concept means explained 82% and 62% of IT concept variance, V1 only 39% and 31%. Ridge from V4 explained 84% and 65% of IT between-concept but only 32% and 30% of within-concept variance; a kernel read-out of V1 added nothing. Thus IT gains semantic concept dimensions, mostly already present in V4, without spectral compression. Limits: multi-unit data, 2 monkeys, unmatched retinotopic coverage, exploratory analyses without a pre-written plan.
